Based on the results concerning defective chromatic polynomials of trees, the family $\{\chi_d(T;k)\}_{d \ge 0}$ determines the number of path subgraphs $P_j$ for $j \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$, while there exist non-isomorphic trees with identical defective chromatic polynomials for all $d \ge 0$ that have different numbers of $P_7$ subgraphs. Thus, $j_{\max} = 6$.
